# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 110 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 110 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_110_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9 — The Commission to Write

**1** A few days later the Shepherd came back and asked me, "Haven't I given you all the commandments and parables?" "You have, Lord," I said. **2** "Then why haven't you acted on them? You need them." "Lord," I said, "there are so many of them — I don't know what's holding me back. I keep trying but I can't seem to follow through." **3** "If you don't fulfill them, you'll lose your salvation. I was sent specifically to save you. But you haven't done what I've told you. **4** If you live by my commandments, you will be saved — and so will everyone else who lives by them. They will have life forever." **5** "Lord," I said, "I'll do everything you've commanded. I know you were sent here for my salvation." **6** "These things are not just for you — they must be kept by everyone who believes in the Lord their God and walks in his commandments." **7** Then he wrote out all the commandments and parables in a book. And he told me: "Write all these commandments and the parables I've shared with you, and also the visions you've seen from the very beginning." **8** Then he left. I wept and prayed to the Lord, asking him to forgive my past sins and to complete in me everything he had shown me through the holy Shepherd. **9** The Lord heard my prayer and answered me with words of grace and comfort.

---

*PNEUMA renders the self-referential writing commission with directness — this moment is where the Shepherd claims its own authorial origin.*
